sun_pixel_position — GEOCAM sun op

• Data kinds: image2d → keypoints

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sun_pixel_position(image, threshold=0.98, min_area=4) (to call the implementation directly, import geocam; geocam.sun_pixel_position(image, threshold=0.98, min_area=4); from the registry, opsgeocam.get("sun_pixel_position"))

Usage

Centroid of the sun in the image (a disk that saturates the sensor) → keypoints (1, 2) = (u, v).

The premise is "the sun saturates the sensor; clouds and snow stop short of saturation". Pixels whose value is at least threshold (absolute, image is 0 to 1) are connected in the 8-neighbourhood, and the luminance centroid of the largest blob is returned. If the blob is smaller than min_area, or there are no saturated pixels, it is "the sun is not in the picture" and raises ValueError (it does not silently return a cloud reflection -- a gate so that, in photos taken when the sun is hidden behind a mountain, a cloud is not read as the sun and does not corrupt the pose). It is not a ratio to the image maximum (with a ratio, in a photo without the sun the brightest cloud would always become "the sun"). Artificial light sources in night scenes and reflections of the sun on water can saturate, so it cannot be used in those scenes. The blob must be a compact disc (fill fraction ≥ 0.4, aspect ratio ≤ 2.5) -- a photo where an overexposed band of sky is saturated gives an elongated blob and is rejected.

Args:

image: (H, W) float, 0 to 1 (out of range is ValueError).

threshold: absolute value regarded as saturation (default 0.98).

min_area: minimum pixel count of a blob.

Returns:

keypoints (1, 2) float: (u, v).
